observations:
The criterion for proposing a new package is: 3 or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language in the source text forming an independent domain not covered by existing packages. Torah #231 does not meet this criterion for the following reasons:

1. BECHINA LANGUAGE ABSENT: The entire two-paragraph text was read carefully. Not a single instance of 'בְּחִינַת', 'נקרא', 'כנ"ל', or any other bechina-marker appears. Every conceptual link in the text is introduced by causal language: 'כִּי כָל הָרְפוּאוֹת עַל יְדֵי כֹּחוֹת הַגַּלְגַּלִּים' (for all healings [come] through the forces of the spheres), 'מֵהֶם מְקַבְּלִים הַסַּמִּים כֹּחַ לְרַפֵּאוֹת' (from them the herbs receive power to heal), 'שֶׁיַּמְשִׁיכוּ אֵלּוּ הַכֹּחוֹת... בְּתוֹךְ חֲתִיכַת לֶחֶם' (that they should draw these forces into a piece of bread). These are eitza (cause-and-effect) flows, not bechina (shared-nature) identities.

2. STRUCTURE OF THE TEACHING: Torah #231 is a practical teaching (halacha lemaaseh) — when to pray and how to frame the request — rather than a metaphysical exposition that maps concept-families onto each other. Its logic is: [cosmic structure] → [therefore pray at this moment] → [God commands → healing flows into food → person heals]. The arrow '→' at every step is eitza, not bechina.

3. RELATIONSHIP TO LM TINYANA 1: The text explicitly cross-references 'לִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא בְּסִימָן א' for the extended treatment. The bechina network for these concepts (celestial forces, healing, prayer, etc.) is developed there, not here. Any package proposals derived from this theme should be assigned to LM2:1.

4. CONCLUSION: No new packages are warranted for Torah #231. The existing dataset contains zero bechina edges for this reference, and the source text confirms this is correct — there are no bechina connections to encode.
